story_assessments.story_title: OpenAI Presence turns agents into a managed workplace product
story_assessments.target_audience: Small business owners, team leads, operations managers, and creators who want AI to save time without losing control.
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want a practical way to use AI inside real work without creating approval, security, or escalation problems.
story_assessments.interest_signal: OpenAI says Presence is available to eligible enterprise customers, and deployments are led by engineers and systems integrators.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It answers the concrete question of how AI moves from chat to a governed workflow.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: See what a managed AI agent looks like and what to define before automating a real task.
story_assessments.proof_point: OpenAI says Presence is available today to eligible enterprise customers through a limited general availability program, with approvals, guardrails, and human escalation built into deployment.
story_assessments.score_reason: Strongest mix of concrete workplace consequence, clear verified detail, and easy-to-explain shift from chat tools to managed systems.

story_assessments.story_title: Google’s ATLAS report shows where AI is actually being used at work
story_assessments.target_audience: Workers, creators, analysts, and managers who want a data-backed view of current AI use.
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want to know what people really do with AI at work, beyond hype or demos.
story_assessments.interest_signal: Google says ATLAS v1.0 is built from 15 million aggregated and de-identified interactions across Gemini products.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It gives a broad snapshot of workplace AI use across countries, languages, occupations, and tasks.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: See which tasks dominate current AI use and where first-use cases cluster.
story_assessments.proof_point: Google says the dataset spans more than 150 countries, 140 languages, 800 occupations, and 4,000 tasks.
story_assessments.score_reason: Useful and credible, but less immediately punchy than the managed-workflow or productivity-gain stories.

story_assessments.story_title: Gallup’s latest workplace data says adoption is widening, but use is still uneven
story_assessments.target_audience: Managers, small business owners, and employees choosing which AI task to test first.
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want AI to produce real productivity gains, not just more tool usage.
story_assessments.interest_signal: Gallup says more than half of U.S. workers now use AI in their role, with writing, research, and problem-solving leading usage.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It ties adoption to specific job functions and measurable payoff.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Identify a task that is frequent, boring, and easy to review, then pilot AI there first.
story_assessments.proof_point: Gallup says the strongest productivity gains are linked to more task-specific uses such as coding, automation, analytics, and slide creation.
story_assessments.score_reason: Most directly actionable for a broad work audience because it links adoption to a simple pilot choice and measurable outcomes.

story_assessments.story_title: The UK is starting to treat AI training as a workplace capability issue
story_assessments.target_audience: Employers, HR leads, operations managers, and small business owners who need a simple AI training plan.
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They need to train staff safely and effectively instead of leaving AI use to ad hoc experimentation.
story_assessments.interest_signal: The UK government says AI is becoming embedded in everyday working life and proposes PRIMES for workforce training.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It turns AI from a software purchase into a training and role-design problem.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Set a simple internal policy, choose approved tools, and run a short training session around one workflow.
story_assessments.proof_point: The UK government says the SKAI programme proposes PRIMES as a framework for inclusive, safe, and sustainable AI workforce training.
story_assessments.score_reason: Practical and credible, with strong employer relevance, though it is narrower and less visually immediate than the top two stories.

tiktok.story_title: OpenAI Presence turns agents into a managed workplace product
tiktok.target_audience: Small business owners, team leads, operations managers, and creators who want AI to save time without losing control.
tiktok.opening: Can AI agents run a work task?
tiktok.payoff: OpenAI says Presence is available to eligible enterprise customers, with guardrails and human escalation built in, so teams can pilot one workflow safely.
tiktok.selection_reason: Best controlled TikTok story: it introduces an unfamiliar capability, a real workplace consequence, and a clear before/after in one beat.

youtube.target_audience: Managers, small business owners, and employees choosing which AI task to test first.
youtube.opening: Which AI task saves time for your team?
youtube.payoff: Gallup says more than half of U.S. workers use AI, and the biggest gains come from task-specific uses like coding, automation, analytics and slides.
youtube.selection_reason: Strong search-friendly Shorts topic with a simple operational takeaway and an easy comparison viewers can answer quickly.

facebook.story_title: Google’s ATLAS report shows where AI is actually being used at work
facebook.target_audience: Workers, creators, analysts, and managers who want a data-backed view of current AI use.
facebook.opening: How do you use AI at work today?
facebook.payoff: Google’s ATLAS report is built from 15 million de-identified interactions, and its early findings suggest workplace AI is mostly being used for collaboration, ideation, information retrieval and learning.
facebook.selection_reason: Good Facebook fit because it feels familiar, data-backed, and easy to answer from personal experience without requiring niche context.

pinterest.story_title: The UK is starting to treat AI training as a workplace capability issue
pinterest.target_audience: Employers, HR leads, operations managers, and small business owners who need a simple AI training plan.
pinterest.opening: AI Upkilling at Work: A Simple Training Checklist for Employers
pinterest.payoff: Use the SKAI direction to build a simple internal AI policy, choose approved tools, and run a short training session around one real workflow.
pinterest.selection_reason: Pinterest works best as a searchable guide, and this story naturally becomes a checklist or policy template for workplace AI training.

linkedin.story_title: OpenAI Presence turns agents into a managed workplace product
linkedin.target_audience: Small business leaders, operations managers, and workplace decision-makers who need governed AI deployment.
linkedin.opening: Can your team approve AI actions before they happen?
linkedin.payoff: OpenAI says Presence is deployed with permissions, guardrails and human escalation, which makes the operational lesson clear: define review rules before you automate a real workflow.
linkedin.selection_reason: Best LinkedIn story because it turns AI into a management decision about accountability, deployment and workflow control.

overall_reasoning: The evidence points to one clear theme: AI at work is moving from experimentation to managed, reviewable workflows. For short-form attention, the strongest hook is the shift from chat to governed agents; for broader platforms, the best response is practical and task-specific. The selections favor stories that let a stranger answer with a real workflow, a real team decision, or a real training need without needing extra context.
